implemented_requirements.evidence: config.DIFFICULTIES defines Beginner (9x9,10), Intermediate (16x16,40), Expert (16x30,99) and GUI selects them via menu.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can uncover cells by clicking
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGUI._on_left_click calls Board.reveal_cell and refreshes the board.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board._calculate_adjacent_mines computes adjacent_mines; GUI displays the number in _refresh_cell.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Uncovering a mine ends the game with a loss
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board.reveal_cell sets game_over and exploded_cell when a mine is revealed; GUI shows loss face and reveals all mines.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Board updates visually after each move
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGUI._refresh_board/_refresh_cell redraws all buttons after each action.
Board.toggle_flag toggles is_flagged; GUI right‑click calls this and updates visual.
Flagged cells use config.SYMBOL_FLAG and config.COLOR_FLAGGED; wrong flags use a different color and symbol.

critical_issues: None observed in the provided code. Minor concerns such as lack of explicit error handling for Tkinter widget creation, but they do not prevent core functionality.
judge.summary: The repository contains a complete Minesweeper implementation with three difficulty presets, cell uncovering, numeric hints, loss on mine, flagging with distinct visuals, and a functional Tkinter UI. All core requirements are met and the code appears ready to run.
